Introduction

Revision Questions

Deep Learning is defined as a type of machine learning (the process of computers improving their own ability to perform tasks by analysing new data) that uses many layers of data processing.

It is a more complex form of traditional machine learning involving a larger range of neurons and layers, introducing a much greater complexity.

Deep Learning vs Traditional Machine Learning

Architecture

  • Traditional networks have a simpler architecture involving only one (or no) hidden layers.
  • Deep learning models consist of deeper neural networks with multiple hidden layers and greater interconnectivity.

Feature Detection

  • Traditional models rely on straightforward techniques and manual feature extraction, such as decision trees and KNN.
  • Deep learning models can automatically detect and learn features without any built-in feature extraction techniques.

Input/Training Data

  • Traditional models can work well with both small and large datasets, with common uses being on smaller sets.
  • Deep learning models require much larger amounts of data in order to learn complex patterns in a non-manual fashion.

Problem-Solving Abilities

  • Traditional models are useful for problems with a limited range of inputs such as simple classifiers. A greater knowledge of the problem domain may also be required to train these models.
  • Deep learning models work better for large quantities of complex input data, such as image and sound. This makes them better in the analysis of speech, language, imagery and audio.

Distinguishing between traditional machine learning and deep learning can be arbitrary and dependent on the task at hand. Whilst models have distinguishing features, the definition of what counts as 'deep' learning and what does not is often a common cause of debate.

Computer Vision

Definition by ChatGPT
  • Computer Vision is a field within artificial intelligence that enables computers to interpret and understand the visual world.
  • Using digital images from cameras and videos and deep learning models, computer vision systems can accurately identify and classify objects, and react to what is seen.
  • This technology is built on the processing and analysis of image data, followed by the use of algorithms to recognize patterns and make decisions.
  • Applications of computer vision are widespread and growing, ranging from safety-enhancing features in autonomous vehicles to automated image diagnostics in healthcare, facial recognition systems, and much more.
  • This field combines machine learning and pattern recognition to bridge the gap between human sight and machine perception.
  • Computer Vision tasks will typically utilise deep learning approaches.

Common Computer Vision Applications

  • Image Classification
  • Object Detection
  • Segmentation
  • Face Recognition
  • Style Transfer
  • Super-Resolution
  • Image Synthesis
  • Pose Estimation
  • OCR (Optical Character Recognition)
